content_voiceover: This is the first-line therapy algorithm for stage one and two DLBCL, excluding stage two with extensive mesenteric disease. The first branch point is bulk, nonbulky meaning less than seven point five centimeters versus bulky at seven point five centimeters or greater. The second branch point is the stage-modified International Prognostic Index, the smIPI, which is built from age over sixty, elevated LDH, poor performance status, and stage two or IIE disease, with zero to one point called low risk and two to four called high risk. For nonbulky, low-risk smIPI disease, the pathway is short, R-CHOP for three cycles, then interim restaging with PET-CT. If that PET is negative, you either give one more cycle of R-CHOP for a total of four, or you consolidate with involved-site radiotherapy and then observe. Nonbulky high-risk smIPI disease gets rerouted to follow the same pathway as stage two with extensive mesenteric disease or stage three-four. Bulky, low-risk disease gets a slightly longer course, R-CHOP for three to four cycles, then interim PET-CT restaging. And stage two with extensive mesenteric disease, or stage three-four disease, goes straight to the suggested regimens table for first-line therapy, followed by interim restaging with PET-CT or CT after two to four cycles.
keypoints: Two branch points: bulk (<7.5cm vs ≥7.5cm) and stage-modified IPI (0-1 low vs 2-4 high)
smIPI factors: age >60, LDH elevated, poor performance status, stage II/IIE
Nonbulky, smIPI 0-1: R-CHOP x3 → interim PET/CT → PET negative gets R-CHOP x1 more or ISRT then observe
Bulky, smIPI 0-1: R-CHOP x3-4 → interim PET/CT restaging
smIPI >1, extensive mesenteric disease, or stage III-IV all follow the same higher-risk pathway
keypoint_voiceover: Remember the two branch points, bulk versus nonbulky at the seven point five centimeter cutoff, and the stage-modified IPI, which is age over sixty, elevated LDH, poor performance status, and stage two or IIE disease. Low risk is zero to one factor, high risk is two to four. Nonbulky, low-risk patients get the shortest course, R-CHOP times three, then interim PET-CT, and if negative, just one more cycle or radiotherapy and observation. Bulky, low-risk patients get three to four cycles before restaging. Anyone with high-risk smIPI, extensive mesenteric disease, or stage three-four disease funnels into the higher-risk pathway with the suggested regimens table.
